pr_title: [Fix #13532] Fix `Lint/NumericOperationWithConstantResult` cop not to complain about `% 1` operation
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/issues/13532

That's clearly not true that `%numeric == 0 (mod 1)` in general:

```
docker run -it --rm rubylang/all-ruby env ALL_RUBY_SINCE=ruby-2.2.0 ./all-ruby -e 'p(1.42 % 1)'
ruby-2.2.0          0.41999999999999993
...
ruby-3.4.0-preview2 0.41999999999999993
```

Thus it makes sense not to complain about `% 1` or `%= 1` at all.

pr_comments:
@koic There's the same issue with `x % x`:

```
irb(main):001> f = 1; f % f
=> 0
irb(main):002> f = 1.1; f % f
=> 0.0
```

Should I address it the same way in a separate PR?
Which cop does that issue pertain to? It would be helpful if you could provide a bit more context.

For instance,

```ruby
def x
  1.618
end

p(x % x)
```

is corrected by `Lint/NumericOperationWithConstantResult` to

```ruby
def x
  1.618
end

p(0)
```

while the result is `0.0`

> There's the same issue with x % x

The same would also be true for `x - x`. I can see why someone would write `x % 1` but is there a usecase for these two cases? Convoluted way to check if a number is a float, I guess. The result may be different but does it actually matter?
These changes make sense to me-- re `x % x`, that should still work when not applied to floats, right? I didn't think enough about floats when making the cop, evidently.

> The same would also be true for x - x. I can see why someone would write x % 1 but is there a usecase for these two cases? Convoluted way to check if a number is a float, I guess. The result may be different but does it actually matter?

Same sentiment here. I'd actually discourage such convoluted checks and suggest some more readable alternatives instead.

So, what should we do here? Leave things as-is? Or disable autocorrection for *some* numeric operations? Or something else? 🙂 

Also, see related https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/issues/13557
I openend https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/pull/13577 to discuss about it
Sorry, I forgot about that you already made this PR when I was amending #13577. I removed both `-` and `%` handling in its entirety in that PR.

issue_context.title: Lint/NumericOperationWithConstantResult incorrectly handles i % 1
issue_context.body:
--------

## Expected behavior
input: 
```ruby
if i % 1 == 0
```
output:
```ruby
if i % 1 == 0
```
## Actual behavior
input: 
```ruby
if i % 1 == 0
```
output:
```ruby
if 0 == 0
```

## Steps to reproduce the problem

`i % 1 == 0` is a valid way to determine if a numeric value has a fractional value:
```ruby
> 1 % 1 == 0
=> true
> 1.0 % 1 == 0
=> true
> 1.1 % 1 == 0
=> false
```

but the autofix from `Lint/NumericOperationWithConstantResult` breaks this. 
```
$ cat foo.rb
if i % 1 == 0

end
$ rubocop -A foo.rb
Inspecting 1 file
W

Offenses:

foo.rb:3:4: W: Lint/BinaryOperatorWithIdenticalOperands: Binary operator == has identical operands.
if 0 == 0
   ^^^^^^

1 file inspected, 1 offense detected

$ cat foo.rb
if 0 == 0

end
```

## RuboCop version


```
1.69.0 (using Parser 3.3.6.0, rubocop-ast 1.36.2, analyzing as Ruby 3.3, running on ruby 3.3.5) [arm64-darwin24]
  - rubocop-factory_bot 2.26.1
  - rubocop-performance 1.23.0
  - rubocop-rails 2.27.0
  - rubocop-rspec 3.2.0
  - rubocop-rspec_rails 2.30.0```
comments:
I agree this is a bug. Cop description says

> Additionally, a variable modulo 0 or itself will always return 0.

(I believe "a variable modulo 1" was meant)

which is simply not true.

review_comments: To prevent it from becoming an incorrect behavior again, can you replace `expect_offense` with `expect_no_offenses` instead of removing the test?
